rationale: The book's identification of lamp oil as the commandment's truth and correction laid up inwardly (producing proven obedience that burns into visible light) accounts for the full supplied network of texts, distinctions, and parable mechanics with fewer unsupported leaps than the Holy Spirit reading. It begins from explicit OT definitions (commandment as lamp, reproof as oil) already linking the exact terms, respects the inventory separation of lamp oil from anointing oil, and explains why the oil must be bought, stored in advance in one's own vessel, and cannot be shared—features that create direct contradictions for a Spirit identification. The Spirit remains the efficient cause (Ezek 36:27) without being collapsed into the fuel itself. No rival core better unifies the same details.
book_core_identification: Lamp oil is the commandment's truth and correction received and laid up inwardly until they govern the life (the tested fruit of the Spirit stored as proven obedience).
book_secondary_elaborations: Light is that same obedience made visible as an example (Matt 5:16).
The oil is 'pressed' fruit (olive crushed under testing, as at Gethsemane) rather than the Spirit himself.
Purchase language means hearing and doing the law (Prov 23:23; Isa 55:1-3), never silver.
Zechariah's oil supplies the lamp while the Spirit empowers the appointed workers who complete the temple.
Foolishness is hearing without doing (Matt 7 parallel), not absence of the Spirit as a discrete gift.
strongest_counter_interpretation: Lamp oil symbolizes the Holy Spirit (indwelling presence, anointing, or empowering that keeps spiritual light burning), drawn from Zechariah 4's Spirit-powered lampstand, the broader oil-Spirit association in anointing texts, and popular exposition of the ten virgins.
counter_core_identification: The Holy Spirit himself (or the Spirit's indwelling/empowering presence) is the oil.
material_core_denial: The oil is not the Spirit (or the Spirit's presence) but the fruit/obedience the Spirit produces and stores; equating the two collapses the cause with its effect and confuses lamp oil with anointing oil.
counter_case: Zechariah 4:6 links the continuously supplied lampstand to 'not by might... but by my Spirit,' inviting identification of the oil with the Spirit.
Anointing oil regularly accompanies the Spirit's coming (1 Sam 16:13; Acts 10:38; Isa 61:1), so oil becomes a natural Spirit symbol transferred to lamp oil.
Exodus 27:20 pure oil for perpetual light is read typologically as Spirit-sustained illumination.
Popular and devotional tradition (especially evangelical/Pentecostal) treats the virgins' oil as genuine Spirit-filled life versus empty profession.
Revelation 4:5 equates burning lamps with the seven spirits of God, reinforcing lamp-Spirit linkage.
book_explanatory_advantages: Direct lexical chain: Prov 6:23 (commandment = lamp, law = light, reproofs of instruction = way of life) + Ps 141:5 (reproof = excellent oil) supplies an explicit OT definition of oil already joined to the lamp/light pair, requiring no transfer from anointing contexts.
Exodus 25:6 / 27:20 / 30:22-33 inventory treats 'oil for the light' and 'spices for anointing oil' as separate provisions with different recipes and uses; the parable uses only the former.

Parable mechanics (oil bought beforehand, stored in personal vessels, finite and non-transferable, refused lest both run short) match a life of accumulated obedience and contradict Spirit-as-gift texts (Acts 8:18-20; John 3:34; Acts 10:44) that allow free, instantaneous, non-diminishing reception.
Proverbs 21:20 already stages wise/foolish + stored oil vs spent oil, matching Matthew 25's vocabulary without remainder.

Jer 31:33 / Ezek 36:27 / Prov 7:1-3 / Ps 119:11 supply the exact inward-writing / heart-storage language the book requires; 1 John 2:4 names the fool who holds the commandment outwardly but lacks the truth within.
Distinguishes cause (Spirit who causes walking in statutes) from effect (the walk/doing stored as oil) without denying the Spirit's role.
counter_explanatory_advantages: Captures the broad biblical oil-Spirit association familiar from anointing narratives and popular preaching.
Zechariah 4's 'by my Spirit' oracle sits next to the oil-fed lampstand, offering a ready (if imprecise) typological bridge.
Explains readiness for the Bridegroom as Spirit-enabled perseverance, a theologically attractive moral.
decisive_sources: Proverbs 6:23 + Psalm 141:5 (lamp-light-oil triad with oil = reproof)
Exodus 25:6; 27:20; 30:22-33 (explicit separation of lamp oil from anointing oil)
Matthew 25:3-9 mechanics (buy, store personally, cannot share, finite reserve)
Proverbs 21:20 (oil stored by wise, spent by fool)
Proverbs 23:23; Psalm 119:11, 151, 172; Jeremiah 31:33; 1 John 2:4 (truth of commandments bought, laid up in heart, governing life)
Ezekiel 36:27 (Spirit as cause of the walk, not the oil itself)
Zechariah 4:6-14 (Spirit empowers the workers; oil is the supply; angel never equates oil with Spirit)
unresolved_objections: Some may still prefer a looser 'preparedness' reading that declines any fixed referent for the oil, though that fails to explain the specific buy/store/share details the book unifies.
The precise 'pressed fruit' imagery, while coherent with olive symbolism and Gethsemane, is an elaboration rather than a bare necessity for the core.
